lessons.title: Costing and Pricing of Logistics Services
lessons.body:
To price your logistics services profitably, you must know your costs. Start by listing all direct costs for a trip: fuel, driver wages, tolls, loading fees, and vehicle maintenance. For example, a trip from Lagos to Ibadan (130 km) might use 40 litres of diesel at â¦1,200 per litre = â¦48,000. Driver wage: â¦10,000. Tolls: â¦2,000. Loading: â¦5,000. Total direct cost: â¦65,000. Now add indirect costs: vehicle insurance, licensing, office rent, and your own salary. If monthly indirect costs are â¦300,000 and you make 20 trips per month, each trip carries â¦15,000 indirect cost. So total cost per trip = â¦80,000. To make a 20% profit, price at â¦96,000. But check competitors: if they charge â¦85,000, you may need to reduce costs or find a niche.

For multiple services, use activity-based costing. For example, if you also offer warehousing, allocate rent, utilities, and labour to storage per pallet. A 100-square-metre warehouse costing â¦200,000 monthly can hold 200 pallets, so each pallet costs â¦1,000 per month. Add handling and admin, then price per pallet.

Always calculate your break-even point. If fixed costs are â¦500,000 monthly and each trip contributes â¦30,000 after variable costs, you need 17 trips to break even. Use simple spreadsheets like Excel or Google Sheets to track costs. Update prices regularly as fuel prices change. In Africa, fuel can fluctuate weekly, so build a fuel surcharge clause into contracts. For cross-border haulage, include customs clearing fees, border delays, and currency exchange costs. Remember, pricing too low kills your business; pricing too high loses customers. Test prices with a few clients before rolling out.

lessons.title: Budgeting and Financial Forecasting
lessons.body:
A budget is a plan for how you will spend and earn money. Start by estimating your income for the next three months. For a logistics business, income comes from trips, storage, and other services. If you have 5 trucks and each does 15 trips monthly at â¦100,000 per trip, monthly income = â¦7,500,000. But be realistic: not all trucks work every day. Use past data or industry averages. Then list expenses: fuel, salaries, rent, maintenance, insurance, loan repayments. For example, fuel might be 40% of income (â¦3,000,000), salaries 20% (â¦1,500,000), maintenance 10% (â¦750,000), rent and utilities 5% (â¦375,000), insurance 3% (â¦225,000), loan repayment 10% (â¦750,000). Total expenses = â¦6,600,000, leaving profit of â¦900,000 (12%).

Forecasting is predicting future income and expenses. Use a simple method: take last year's figures and adjust for growth or inflation. If inflation is 15%, increase costs by 15%. If you plan to buy a new truck, add loan repayments and additional fuel. Create a cash flow forecast: month by month, when cash comes in and goes out. For example, a client may pay 30 days after delivery, so you need enough cash to cover expenses before payment arrives.

Use tools like Excel templates or mobile apps like Wave or QuickBooks. In Africa, where bank loans are expensive, budgeting helps you avoid borrowing. Review your budget monthly. If fuel prices rise, cut non-essential spending. Involve your team: drivers can suggest fuel-saving routes. A good budget is flexible and realistic. Always keep a contingency of 10% for unexpected costs like breakdowns or fines.

lessons.title: Cash Flow Management and Working Capital
lessons.body:
Cash flow is the movement of money in and out of your business. Even if you are profitable on paper, you can run out of cash if clients pay late. For example, you complete a trip worth â¦500,000, but the client pays after 60 days. Meanwhile, you must pay for fuel, driver, and tolls immediately. If you don't have cash reserves, you can't take the next job. Working capital is the money you need to cover day-to-day operations: current assets (cash, receivables, fuel stock) minus current liabilities (payables, short-term loans).

To manage cash flow, invoice promptly and follow up on payments. Offer a 2% discount for early payment (e.g., within 10 days). Use mobile money or bank transfers to speed up receipts. For large clients, request a deposit of 30-50% upfront. Keep a cash flow forecast showing weekly inflows and outflows. If you see a shortfall, arrange an overdraft or delay non-essential purchases. In Africa, where many businesses operate informally, keep a separate bank account for business and personal use.

Build a cash buffer of at least one month's expenses. If monthly expenses are â¦6,000,000, aim to have â¦6,000,000 in reserve. You can also use invoice factoring: sell your unpaid invoices to a financier for a fee (e.g., 5% of invoice value) to get cash quickly. For working capital, negotiate longer payment terms with suppliers (e.g., 30 days) and shorter terms with customers. Monitor your cash conversion cycle: days inventory + days receivables - days payables. If it's too long, you tie up cash. For example, if you hold fuel for 10 days, collect receivables in 45 days, and pay suppliers in 30 days, your cycle is 25 days. Reduce it by collecting faster or paying later.

lessons.title: Investment Appraisal for Logistics Assets
lessons.body:
When buying a new truck, you need to know if it's worth the money. Investment appraisal compares the cost of the asset with the future cash flows it will generate. Simple methods include payback period and return on investment (ROI). For example, a used truck costs â¦15,000,000. It generates â¦500,000 net cash per month (after all expenses). Payback period = â¦15,000,000 / â¦500,000 = 30 months (2.5 years). If you expect the truck to last 5 years, it's a good investment. ROI = (annual net cash / cost) x 100 = (â¦6,000,000 / â¦15,000,000) x 100 = 40% per year. Compare this to leaving money in a bank (e.g., 10% interest) or buying a different asset.

For more accuracy, use net present value (NPV) or internal rate of return (IRR). NPV discounts future cash flows to today's value. If interest rates are 20%, â¦500,000 next year is worth â¦416,667 today. Sum the discounted cash flows over the truck's life and subtract the initial cost. If NPV is positive, invest. IRR is the discount rate that makes NPV zero. If IRR > your cost of capital (e.g., loan interest), invest.

In Africa, consider risks: fuel price volatility, currency devaluation, and political instability. Use a higher discount rate for risky investments. Also consider alternatives: leasing instead of buying, or hiring subcontractors. For example, leasing a truck might cost â¦800,000 per month, but you avoid maintenance and depreciation. Compare total lease cost over 3 years (â¦28,800,000) with buying (â¦15,000,000 + maintenance). Often, buying is cheaper if you have the capital. Always include salvage value: a truck bought for â¦15,000,000 might sell for â¦5,000,000 after 5 years. Use Excel's NPV and IRR functions to calculate. Never invest without a clear payback plan.

lessons.title: Key Financial Metrics and KPIs
lessons.body:
To run a profitable logistics business, track key financial metrics. These are numbers that tell you how well you're doing. Start with gross profit margin: (revenue - direct costs) / revenue x 100. If a trip earns â¦100,000 and direct costs are â¦70,000, gross margin is 30%. Aim for at least 25-30% in logistics. Net profit margin: (revenue - all costs) / revenue x 100. If all costs are â¦90,000, net margin is 10%. Compare with industry averages.

Other important metrics: cost per kilometre. If a truck's monthly costs (fuel, driver, maintenance, insurance) are â¦1,200,000 and it runs 5,000 km, cost per km = â¦240. You can then price per km to ensure profit. Revenue per truck: total revenue / number of trucks. If you have 5 trucks and revenue is â¦7,500,000, each truck earns â¦1,500,000. Track this monthly to see if trucks are underutilised. Fuel efficiency: kilometres per litre. If a truck uses 40 litres for 130 km, efficiency = 3.25 km/l. Improve by driver training and maintenance.

Also monitor days sales outstanding (DSO): average days to collect payment. If DSO is 60 days, you need more working capital. Aim for 30 days. Current ratio: current assets / current liabilities. A ratio above 1.5 is healthy. Debt-to-equity ratio: total debt / equity. Keep it below 2:1 to avoid risk. Use a simple dashboard in Excel or a notebook. Review weekly. In Africa, where cash is king, also track cash balance daily. Set targets: e.g., increase gross margin to 35%, reduce DSO to 45 days. Share metrics with your team and reward improvements. These numbers guide decisions: if cost per km rises, find cheaper fuel or routes.

lessons.title: Risk Management and Insurance
lessons.body:
Logistics is risky: accidents, theft, fuel price spikes, currency changes, and client defaults. Risk management means identifying risks, reducing them, and transferring them through insurance. First, list all risks: vehicle accidents, cargo theft, driver injury, fire, flood, and political unrest. For each, assess likelihood and impact. A major accident could cost â¦10,000,000 in vehicle damage and legal fees. If you can't afford that, you need insurance.

In Africa, common insurances for logistics: commercial vehicle insurance (third party, fire, theft), goods in transit insurance (covers cargo), and workers' compensation. For a truck worth â¦15,000,000, comprehensive insurance might cost â¦600,000 per year (4% of value). Goods in transit insurance might cost 0.5% of cargo value per trip. For a â¦5,000,000 cargo, that's â¦25,000 per trip. Shop around: use local brokers and compare quotes. Also consider microinsurance for small operators.

Beyond insurance, reduce risk: train drivers in defensive driving, install GPS trackers (cost â¦50,000 per truck) to prevent theft, and do regular maintenance. Diversify clients: don't rely on one big customer. Keep contracts clear on liability and payment terms. For cross-border, buy political risk insurance or use letters of credit. Build an emergency fund: 3-6 months of expenses. If a truck breaks down, you can repair it without borrowing. Also have a business continuity plan: if a key driver leaves, who replaces them? Document procedures. In Africa, where insurance claims can be slow, keep copies of all documents and photos of incidents. Work with a reputable insurer. Finally, review risks quarterly and adjust your insurance as your business grows.

quiz.q: What is the first step in costing a logistics service?
options: A) Set a price based on competitors
quiz.explanation: You must know your direct costs (fuel, wages, etc.) before you can price profitably.

quiz.q: If a trip's direct costs are â¦65,000 and indirect costs allocated are â¦15,000, what is the total cost?
quiz.explanation: Total cost = direct costs + indirect costs = â¦65,000 + â¦15,000 = â¦80,000.

quiz.q: What is break-even point?
options: A) The price at which you make maximum profit
B) The number of trips needed to cover all costs
C) The cost of fuel per trip
D) The total revenue minus total costs
quiz.explanation: Break-even is when total revenue equals total costs, so you need enough trips to cover fixed and variable costs.

quiz.q: Why should you include a fuel surcharge clause in contracts?
quiz.explanation: Fuel prices can change frequently, so a surcharge protects your profit margin.

quiz.q: What is a budget?
options: A) A record of past expenses
B) A plan for future income and expenses
C) A loan from a bank
quiz.explanation: A budget is a forward-looking plan for how you will earn and spend money.

quiz.q: If monthly income is â¦7,500,000 and expenses are â¦6,600,000, what is the profit?
What is forecasting?
quiz.explanation: Forecasting uses past data and assumptions to predict future income and expenses.

quiz.q: Why is a cash flow forecast important?
options: B) To ensure you have cash when needed
quiz.explanation: Cash flow forecast helps you anticipate shortfalls and avoid running out of money.

quiz.q: What is working capital?
options: B) Current assets minus current liabilities
C) Total revenue minus total costs
D) The value of your trucks
quiz.explanation: Working capital measures short-term financial health and ability to cover day-to-day operations.

quiz.q: How can you speed up cash inflows?
options: A) Offer discounts for early payment
quiz.explanation: Early payment discounts encourage customers to pay faster, improving cash flow.

quiz.q: What is a cash buffer?
options: A) A reserve of cash for emergencies
C) A loan from a bank
quiz.explanation: A cash buffer is money set aside to cover unexpected expenses or slow periods.

quiz.q: What is invoice factoring?
options: A) Selling unpaid invoices for cash
quiz.explanation: Invoice factoring gives you immediate cash by selling receivables to a financier at a discount.

quiz.q: What is payback period?
options: A) Time to recover the cost of an investment
B) Time to pay off a loan
C) Time to complete a trip
D) Time to receive payment from clients
quiz.explanation: Payback period is how long it takes for an investment's cash flows to equal its initial cost.

quiz.q: If a truck costs â¦15,000,000 and generates â¦500,000 net cash per month, what is the payback period?
quiz.explanation: Payback = cost / monthly cash flow = â¦15,000,000 / â¦500,000 = 30 months.

quiz.q: What does a positive NPV indicate?
options: A) The investment is not profitable
D) The investment should be delayed
quiz.explanation: A positive NPV means the present value of future cash flows exceeds the initial cost.

quiz.q: Why might you use a higher discount rate for investments in Africa?
options: A) To account for higher risk
quiz.explanation: Higher risk (e.g., political instability) requires a higher discount rate to reflect uncertainty.

quiz.q: What is salvage value?
options: B) The resale value of an asset at the end of its life
quiz.explanation: Salvage value is the estimated amount you can sell an asset for after its useful life.

quiz.q: What is gross profit margin?
quiz.explanation: Gross profit margin measures profitability after accounting for direct costs of services.

quiz.q: If revenue is â¦100,000 and direct costs are â¦70,000, what is the gross profit margin?
What does cost per kilometre help you determine?
quiz.explanation: Knowing cost per km allows you to set a profitable price per km for trips.

quiz.q: What is days sales outstanding (DSO)?
options: A) Average days to collect payment from customers
B) Average days to pay suppliers
C) Average days to complete a trip
D) Average days to sell inventory
quiz.explanation: DSO measures how long it takes to convert sales into cash.

quiz.q: What is a healthy current ratio?
quiz.explanation: A current ratio above 1.5 indicates good short-term financial health.

quiz.q: What is the debt-to-equity ratio?
quiz.explanation: Debt-to-equity shows the proportion of debt used to finance assets relative to equity.

quiz.q: What is risk management?
options: B) Identifying, reducing, and transferring risks
quiz.explanation: Risk management is a proactive process to handle uncertainties that could harm the business.

quiz.q: Which insurance covers cargo during transit?
quiz.explanation: Goods in transit insurance specifically covers cargo while being transported.

quiz.q: If a truck is worth â¦15,000,000 and comprehensive insurance costs 4% per year, what is the annual premium?
How can you reduce risk of theft?
quiz.explanation: GPS trackers help monitor vehicle location and deter theft.

quiz.q: Why is diversifying clients important?
options: B) To reduce dependence on one customer
D) To get better insurance rates
quiz.explanation: If one client defaults, having multiple clients reduces the impact on your business.

quiz.q: What is an emergency fund?
options: A) Money set aside for unexpected expenses
B) A loan from a bank
D) A savings account for retirement
quiz.explanation: An emergency fund provides cash to handle unforeseen events like breakdowns.

quiz.q: What should you do after a vehicle accident?
options: B) Take photos and document everything
quiz.explanation: Documenting the incident with photos and details is crucial for insurance claims.
